title: Guide - Peace in the Psalms - I lift my eyes

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, steady and unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Peace in the Psalms. <short pause> This reading is called I Lift My Eyes. <short pause> We'll listen to Psalm one hundred twenty-one. <short pause> It is a short psalm, made for people on the way... <short pause> so you can come to it in the middle of things.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Wherever you are, let your eyes soften. <short pause> When we worry, our looking grows narrow. <short pause> We stare at the screen, the floor, the problem just in front of us. <short pause> If you can, look up for a moment... <short pause> to a window, a ceiling, a piece of sky. <short pause> Or simply lift your attention.

This is one of the Songs of Ascents, psalms that travelers may have sung as they climbed toward Jerusalem. <short pause> The road was long, with loose stones underfoot, hot sun, and hills where danger could hide. <short pause> It begins with an honest question... <short pause> where will my help come from?
I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help. <short pause> My help cometh from the Lord, which made heaven and earth.

He will not suffer thy foot to be moved: he that keepeth thee will not slumber. <short pause> Behold, he that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep. <short pause> The Lord is thy keeper: the Lord is thy shade upon thy right hand. <short pause> The sun shall not smite thee by day, nor the moon by night.
The Lord shall preserve thee from all evil: he shall preserve thy soul. <short pause> The Lord shall preserve thy going out and thy coming in from this time forth, and even for evermore.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: My help cometh from the Lord, which made heaven and earth. <short pause> The traveler looks at the hills, and then past them, to the One who made the hills. <short pause> What is in front of you may be very large. <short pause> It is not larger than its Maker.

And did you hear how often this psalm says that you are kept? <short pause> He keepeth. Thy keeper. He shall preserve. <short pause> In the Hebrew, it is the same word again and again, six times in eight short verses. <short pause> As though the singer knew that a worried heart needs to be told more than once.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: So let yourself be told again. <short pause> Your foot is kept, on uncertain ground. <short pause> Your days are kept, under a hard sun. <short pause> Your nights are kept, under the moon. <short pause> Your going out is kept. <short pause> Your coming in is kept. <short pause> Your soul is kept.

parts.style: gentle, a soft smile in the voice, illustrating
parts.text: He does not slumber. <short pause> Think of what that means for you. <short pause> You don't have to be the one who watches every hour. <short pause> You can close your eyes, or turn your back on the problem for a while... <short pause> and nothing you love will be left without a keeper.

Being kept doesn't mean the road has no stones. <short pause> You may still stumble, and some days will hurt. <short pause> It means you are never unattended on it. <short pause> From this time forth, the psalm says... <short pause> which means beginning now, right where you are standing.

Is there a going out ahead of you, something you must walk into? <short pause> Or a person whose coming and going you worry over? <short pause> Picture that doorway now. <short pause> And picture the Lord already standing in it... <short pause> keeping the going out, and the coming in.

Let's pray. <short pause> Maker of heaven and earth, <short pause> lift my eyes from what frightens me to the One who helps me. <short pause> Watch over my steps today, and over the ones I love where I cannot follow them. <short pause> When I am too tired to keep watch, thank You that You never are. <short pause> Amen.
The next time you pass through a door, let it remind you. <short pause> Going out, and coming in... <short pause> I am kept. <short pause> Lift your eyes, and go gently.
